goal: Add a "REQUEST WX" datalink feature: a new flight-scoped endpoint that looks up METAR/TAF for an ICAO from a public, no-auth weather source, files a downlink WX REQUEST + uplink METAR/TAF reply (or an uplink WX DATA UNAVAILABLE rejection) into the flight's acars_messages thread using the frozen acars_message_center substrate (no schema migration), caches upstream responses briefly per ICAO in-process to avoid hammering the source, and adds a REQUEST WX action to client/src/pages/AcarsMessages.tsx that defaults its ICAO field from the active planned leg's departure/destination. The MCDU client (oshogun/msfslogger_mcdu) is out of scope.
frozen_decisions: Direction convention (from acars_message_center design §3.2, binding on this run): a crew-initiated request is `downlink`; the ground's/system's answer is `uplink`. WX REQUEST <ICAO> is downlink; the METAR/TAF reply and the WX DATA UNAVAILABLE rejection are both uplink. This overrides user_stories/acars_weather_request.md's own prose, which has the direction backwards.
Flight-scoped, not leg-scoped: weather isn't tied to a specific leg's dispatch data, and a crew can request weather for any ICAO (e.g. an alternate) unrelated to the leg's departure/destination.

No schema migration. acars_message_center design freezes the acars_messages columns as sufficient for every sibling story including this one (design §3.1 already gives the wx row shapes); a new column is a defect to raise there, not to add here.

wx rows carry no dedup_key (acars_message_center design §3.1): every REQUEST WX call logs a new downlink request row and a new uplink reply/rejection row, even on a cache hit. Only the upstream fetch itself is deduped, by the in-process TTL cache — the cache and the database dedup mechanism (insertAcarsMessageOnce) are two different things and this run uses only the former.

Upstream weather source is expected to need no API key/credential, matching src/simbriefClient.ts's stance toward SimBrief. If the Designer's chosen source turns out to need one, that is escalated back to the Orchestrator before Implement — it is not a reason for the Planner or Designer to add a DevOps task unilaterally.
No DevOps/Ship task this run: no build, packaging, deploy, CI or secrets change is expected.

The web client is the only client in scope. client/src/pages/AcarsMessages.tsx already reads plannedLegId from the thread response; it does not currently expose departure/destination ICAO strings, and the Designer must specify what the page fetches to get them.
sequencing_rationale: One phase, matching the sibling run 2026-09-14-acars-dispatch-loadsheet's shape exactly: this is a single coherent feature built entirely on an already-frozen substrate, with one new contract (the weather client + cache + endpoint) to freeze before anyone writes code against it.

Design (T-001) must land before either implementer starts: the upstream source choice, the cache's hit/miss definition, the endpoint's request/response/rejection shapes, and the client's default-ICAO data source are all genuinely undecided and would otherwise be guessed independently by backend_sr and frontend_sr and disagree at the seam (the response shape T-003 consumes, the rejection string T-003 renders verbatim).

T-002 (backend_sr) and T-003 (frontend_sr) both depend only on T-001 and touch disjoint file sets (src/** vs client/src/**), so they run in parallel once the design is frozen — same as the sibling run's T-002/T-003.

backend_sr rather than backend_jr for T-002: a new external client module with its own error taxonomy, an in-process cache with its own invalidation rule, and a new route are contract-adjacent work spanning several modules (src/weatherClient.ts, src/acars.ts, src/routes/acars.ts, src/types.ts) — not a single-seam edit.

frontend_sr rather than frontend_jr for T-003: the REQUEST WX action needs a new data dependency (fetching the planned leg's departure/destination) the page does not already hold, plus new client-side state (an ICAO input, its default, and validation feedback) — more than a single self-contained component change.
One reviewer task (T-004) gates both implementers before either is considered mergeable, per the standard loop; it depends on both T-002 and T-003 so a request_changes on either keeps the phase open.

phases.name: REQUEST WX
phases.ships: On the ACARS Messages page for a flight, a REQUEST WX action (ICAO field pre-filled from the active leg's departure/destination when one exists) files a downlink WX REQUEST and, moments later, an uplink METAR/TAF reply (or a WX DATA UNAVAILABLE rejection for an invalid/unfetchable ICAO) into the thread without a page reload. Repeated requests for the same ICAO within the cache window answer from cache rather than re-hitting the upstream source.

tasks.title: Freeze the weather client, the TTL cache, the WX endpoint, and the client's default-ICAO contract
tasks.goal: Produce .claude/runs/2026-09-14-acars-weather-request/design.md deciding, precisely enough that backend_sr and frontend_sr need nothing else: (1) the upstream METAR/TAF source — URL shape, confirm and cite that it needs no API key/auth (matching src/simbriefClient.ts's stance on SimBrief; aviationweather.gov's public Data API at https://aviationweather.gov/data/api/ is a strong candidate — no key required, METAR updates ~1/min, TAF ~1/10min, and its own docs ask callers to keep request frequency low and cache rather than poll, which is exactly what AC3 requires — but confirm current terms before freezing and document the source's usage/rate-limit guidance in design.md, a story requirement); (2) src/weatherClient.ts's exact exported function signature(s), modeled on src/simbriefClient.ts's shape (a typed error class with a machine code, a user-facing message, and an httpStatus/upstreamStatus when known; a request timeout; no bare network/JSON errors escaping); how a raw METAR/TAF response maps to `{icao, metar, taf, fetched_at}` (TAF may legitimately be absent for a station — decide how that's represented) and to the `{icao, reason}` shape for a fetch/parse failure; (3) the in-process TTL cache: keyed by normalised (uppercased) ICAO, a frozen TTL (a few minutes, per the story), an explicit definition of a cache 'hit' for AC3 (a second REQUEST WX call for the same ICAO within the TTL must not invoke the upstream fetch function — state how this is verified, e.g. an injectable fetch/clock and a call-count assertion), confirmation the cache holds only the parsed METAR/TAF (or failure) and is never persisted to acars_messages or any table, and what a cache hit means for the two rows written per call (every call still writes a fresh downlink request row and a fresh uplink reply/rejection row via insertAcarsMessage — no dedup_key exists for wx rows per acars_message_center design §3.1 — only the upstream network call is elided); (4) the endpoint: exact method and path (flight-scoped, POST /api/flights/:id/acars-messages/wx as the sibling of the existing GET/POST /flights/:id/acars-messages and the leg-scoped POST /planned-legs/:legId/acars-messages/loadsheet in src/routes/acars.ts, unless a concrete reason favours a different path), request body `{icao}`, success response shape (mirroring LoadsheetRequestResponse's pattern: the created request and reply AcarsMessage rows plus a parsed convenience payload so the client need not scrape body text), and exactly how ICAO validation works — decide whether a malformed ICAO (not 4 alnum characters after trim/uppercase) is rejected before any row is written (400, no thread entry — a typo is not a WX request the crew made) versus a well-formed ICAO the upstream has no data for or that a fetch failure prevents answering, which files the downlink request row plus the frozen uplink rejection reply with body "WX DATA UNAVAILABLE FOR <ICAO>" (payload_json `{icao, reason}`) and a 200/201 (this is a feature outcome, not a server error — the request+rejection pair is exactly what a real ACARS WX request looks like when the ground can't answer); state whether ICAO shape validation reuses src/airports.ts's `/^[A-Z0-9]{4}$/` pattern (src/airports.ts exports no standalone validator today — confirm) or defines its own in src/acars.ts; (5) the client contract for client/src/pages/AcarsMessages.tsx: the page currently holds only `plannedLegId` (a number) from the thread response — specify that it fetches GET /api/planned-legs/:legId (an existing endpoint returning PlannedLegWithChildren, already used by client/src/pages/FlightDetail.tsx for the same kind of lookup — no server change) to read departure_ident/destination_ident, respecting departure_is_airport/destination_is_airport (a non-airport waypoint has no ICAO to suggest), and specify exactly what the default-ICAO UI affordance is (e.g. two quick-fill buttons or a pre-filled text input) when zero, one, or two of departure/destination are usable airports; specify how the returned request/reply rows are merged into the client's `messages` state given every call writes a fresh pair (no idempotency to reconcile, unlike the loadsheet action — state whether this is a plain append, like handleSend's canned-message append, rather than the loadsheet's merge-by-id); (6) the exact TypeScript types to add to src/types.ts and client/src/types.ts (mirrored by hand, as AcarsMessage/LoadsheetRequestResponse already are) for the WX request/response shapes.
acceptance_criteria: design.md names the exact upstream source (URL/endpoint shape), states and cites that it requires no API key, and documents its usage/rate-limit guidance — if the chosen source turns out to need a key or credential, design.md says so explicitly and flags it as a decision for the Orchestrator rather than silently proceeding.

design.md gives src/weatherClient.ts's exact exported function signature(s), its error taxonomy (codes and what each maps to), and its timeout value, explicitly modeled on or diverging from src/simbriefClient.ts's SimbriefFetchError shape with a stated reason for any divergence.

design.md specifies the cache's key (normalised ICAO), its frozen TTL, an explicit test-observable definition of 'hit' (e.g. an injectable fetch implementation whose call count does not increase on a hit), and confirms every REQUEST WX call still writes a fresh downlink request row and a fresh uplink reply/rejection row regardless of cache hit or miss.

design.md gives the endpoint's exact method, path, request body, success response shape (including a parsed metar/taf/fetched_at convenience payload), and resolves the malformed-ICAO-vs-unfetchable-ICAO distinction with an exact HTTP status and row-written/not-written outcome for each case, plus the literal rejection body text "WX DATA UNAVAILABLE FOR <ICAO>".

design.md states precisely what client/src/pages/AcarsMessages.tsx fetches (confirmed as the existing GET /api/planned-legs/:legId, or an alternative with a stated reason) to obtain departure/destination ICAO, how departure_is_airport/destination_is_airport gate the suggestion, and how the returned rows are merged into client state (append vs merge-by-id), with a reason tied to whether the server response is idempotent.
design.md lists the exact TypeScript type names and shapes to add to src/types.ts and client/src/types.ts.

tasks.title: Build the weather client, TTL cache, and the WX request endpoint
tasks.goal: Per `ctx.sh design 2026-09-14-acars-weather-request <sections frozen by T-001 covering: the upstream source and src/weatherClient.ts's contract, the TTL cache, the endpoint contract, and the ICAO validation split>`: (1) create src/weatherClient.ts, modeled on src/simbriefClient.ts (a typed fetch error class with a machine code and user-facing message, a request timeout, an injectable fetch implementation for tests, no bare network/JSON error escaping) implementing the function signature(s) T-001 froze; (2) implement the in-process TTL cache exactly as T-001 specifies (key, TTL, hit definition) — in src/weatherClient.ts or a sibling module per the design's choice; (3) add ICAO-shape validation and the WX request/reply body formatters/dedup constants (if any) to src/acars.ts, following the existing pure-module conventions (no I/O, no clock — issuedAt stays a parameter) alongside buildLoadsheetRequestBody/buildLoadsheetReplyBody's style; (4) add the endpoint T-001 specifies to src/routes/acars.ts as a sibling of the existing routes, writing the downlink request row via insertAcarsMessage and the uplink reply/rejection row via insertAcarsMessage (not insertAcarsMessageOnce — wx rows carry no dedup_key), correlation_id set to the request row's id; (5) add the TypeScript types T-001 names to src/types.ts. Add a src/inspect-weather.ts ts-node CLI inspector (pattern: src/inspect-simbrief.ts) that takes an ICAO and prints the parsed METAR/TAF or the failure — the cheapest way to eyeball a real fetch against the live upstream without touching flights.db.
acceptance_criteria: `npx tsc --noEmit` passes with the new module, route and type additions in place.

A unit-style exercise of src/weatherClient.ts with an injected fake fetch (a small ts-node script under the session scratchpad, or via `npm test` if T-002 adds a tests/ file — no tests/ path is in allowed_paths so any Vitest coverage is a follow-up, not required here) demonstrates: a successful METAR(+TAF) response parses into the design's shape; a malformed/error upstream response and a simulated timeout both reject with the design's typed error, never a bare exception.

Against a scratch server (PORT=3100+, scratch copy of flights.db) and a real or ts-node-scripted call to the WX endpoint for a real, currently-reporting ICAO (e.g. EGLL or KJFK), the response contains METAR text and the flight's acars_messages thread (`listAcarsMessagesForFlight` via a better-sqlite3 query against the scratch db) gains exactly two new rows: one direction='downlink' category='wx' WX REQUEST row and one direction='uplink' category='wx' reply row whose correlation_id equals the request row's id.

Requesting the same ICAO twice within the cache TTL against the scratch server results in two new request+reply row pairs in the thread (every call is logged) but the injected/instrumented fetch call count to the upstream increases by only one — demonstrated by a scratch-only instrumentation (e.g. a request counter exposed via an env var or a temporary log line counted in the report, removed or gated before merge) proving AC3 (`Requesting the same ICAO twice within the cache window does not issue a second upstream fetch`).

Requesting a malformed ICAO (not 4 alnum characters) and requesting a well-formed but non-existent/unfetchable ICAO (e.g. 'ZZZZ') against the scratch server each produce the design's exact frozen outcome — status code and, for the well-formed case, an uplink row with body exactly "WX DATA UNAVAILABLE FOR ZZZZ" — with no unhandled 500 in either case.
The live flights.db is untouched: report states its md5 is identical before and after this task's work (only a scratch copy was written to).

tasks.title: Add the REQUEST WX action to the web ACARS Messages page
tasks.goal: Per `ctx.sh design 2026-09-14-acars-weather-request <sections frozen by T-001 covering: the endpoint contract, the client's default-ICAO data source, and the client/src/types.ts shape>`: add a REQUEST WX action to client/src/pages/AcarsMessages.tsx — an ICAO input (or the two-button quick-fill T-001 specifies) defaulted from the active leg's departure/destination, fetched via GET /api/planned-legs/:legId (or whatever T-001 froze) alongside the existing thread load, gated the same way the page already gates on missing planned-leg context when there is no linked leg. Submitting POSTs to the WX endpoint T-001 specifies and appends (or merges, per T-001's decision) the returned row(s) into the rendered thread — no refetch. Surface the "WX DATA UNAVAILABLE FOR <ICAO>" rejection and any malformed-ICAO rejection as inline errors via the existing `sendError` pattern, never a thrown/uncaught exception. Add the type(s) T-001 names to client/src/types.ts, mirrored by hand from src/types.ts.
acceptance_criteria: `npm run build` (client) succeeds with no new TypeScript errors.

Against a scratch server, opening the ACARS Messages page for a flight linked to a planned leg with airport departure/destination idents shows the REQUEST WX affordance pre-filled/quick-filled with those ICAOs, per T-001's exact UI contract — screenshotted to the run's scratchpad.

Against the same scratch server, submitting REQUEST WX for a real, currently-reporting ICAO appends a new downlink WX REQUEST row and a new uplink METAR reply row to the rendered thread without a page reload — screenshotted, and re-submitting the same ICAO appends a second fresh pair (not a duplicate-suppressed no-op), matching the design's stated merge behaviour for a non-idempotent endpoint.

Requesting an unfetchable/invalid ICAO against the scratch server renders the literal rejection text the design freezes as an inline error (same pattern as `sendError`), not a thrown error or a blank page — screenshotted.

When the flight has no linked planned leg (`plannedLegId === null` in current page state), the REQUEST WX action still lets a user type an arbitrary ICAO (weather is not restricted to the leg's airports) but shows no default suggestion — verified by a code read confirming the default-fill path is gated separately from the action's overall availability, since AC1 ("a valid ICAO with available weather returns METAR text") must work for a flight with no linked leg at all.

tasks.title: Review phase 1: weather client, cache, WX endpoint, and the web client action
tasks.goal: Review T-002 and T-003 against `ctx.sh design 2026-09-14-acars-weather-request` (the full frozen contract) and this run's acceptance criteria in user_stories/acars_weather_request.md (read with the intake's direction-convention correction applied). Re-run the evidence named in T-002's and T-003's acceptance criteria against a scratch server and a scratch copy of flights.db — never the live server or live flights.db. Specifically check: AC1 (a valid ICAO with available weather returns METAR text in the thread); AC2 (an invalid/unknown ICAO returns a clear rejection, never an unhandled error — try both a malformed ICAO and a well-formed but non-existent one); AC3 (repeated requests for the same ICAO within the TTL do not re-hit the upstream — re-derive the evidence T-002 reported, don't just re-read it); AC4 (the departure/destination default is pre-filled from the active leg when one exists); that wx rows carry no dedup_key and every call logs a fresh request+reply pair (grep the insert calls — insertAcarsMessage, not insertAcarsMessageOnce, for wx rows); that direction is downlink-request/uplink-reply, matching the frozen acars_message_center §3.2 convention; that src/weatherClient.ts sends no credential of any kind (grep for any Authorization header, API key or token); and that a live upstream outage cannot 500 the endpoint (simulate by pointing the client at an unreachable host via its test seam, if one exists, or by reviewing the catch path).
acceptance_criteria: Every acceptance criterion listed on T-002 and T-003 is independently re-verified (command re-run, not just re-read) and passes.

The four acceptance criteria in user_stories/acars_weather_request.md are each traced to a passing check: AC1 (valid ICAO returns METAR text), AC2 (invalid/unknown ICAO returns a clear rejection, not an unhandled error), AC3 (repeated requests within the cache window issue only one upstream fetch), AC4 (departure/destination pre-filled from the active leg).
`npx tsc` (server) and `npm run build` (client) both succeed.
`npm test` still passes unchanged.
src/weatherClient.ts sends no API key, token or credential of any kind, confirmed by reading the request construction, not merely by the design doc's claim.
Verdict is `approve` or `request_changes` with concrete, file-and-line feedback; on `request_changes`, the task returns to the same implementer (T-002 or T-003) that owns the affected file.
